title: CI Observe — Where the time goes
description: Where E2E run time goes: phases, steps, the runner wait, slow tests and product waits.

options.content: **Where E2E time goes.** A run waits for a runner, sets up CI, brings up a cluster and hosts, builds, installs OSAC, runs the tests and collects logs. Phases and steps are measured on **passing** runs (a failed run stops early); hours and the runner wait count every run. *Inside the tests* shows what the tests themselves spend their time on, and what they wait for in the product.

panels.title: Typical time to result
panels.description: Median, from the first job's creation to the last job's end. Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Slow runs take
panels.description: The 90th percentile: 9 in 10 passing runs finish faster. Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Average passing run
panels.description: The mean passing run. Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Typical wait for a runner
panels.description: Median wait for a self-hosted runner. Population: finished suite runs with a stored job timeline (runs stored before timelines existed have no runner wait). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Runner hours
panels.description: Wall-clock hours of every finished run. Population: finished VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs (passed, failed or cancelled). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: hours.

panels.title: Hours on failed runs
panels.description: Share of the runner hours spent on runs that failed. Population: finished VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs (passed, failed or cancelled). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent of hours.

panels.title: A passing run, phase by phase
panels.description: The average passing run of each suite: the wait for a runner, then each group of workflow steps (in every job of the run). Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Phases
panels.description: Each phase of a passing run: its average, median and slow (p90) duration, its share of the average run, and how its average moved. Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above); 'vs before' compares with the $days days before. Unit: duration and percent.

panels.title: Phase time per day
panels.description: The average passing run per day, stacked by phase: a band that grows is a phase getting slower. Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: one point per UTC day the runs were created, last $days days. Unit: duration.

panels.title: Wait for a runner per day
panels.description: Median and slow (p90) wait for a self-hosted runner per day. Population: finished suite runs with a stored job timeline (runs stored before timelines existed have no runner wait). Time: one point per UTC day the runs were created, last $days days. Unit: duration.

panels.title: Steps
panels.description: Every workflow step of a passing run, the biggest share first. Share: of the average run. 'vs before': the median compared with the previous window; red means slower. Population: passing VMaaS, CaaS and BMaaS suite runs. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above); 'vs before' compares with the $days days before. Unit: duration and percent.

panels.title: Where the tests' time goes
panels.description: The recorded tests' own time, split four ways: setup (fixtures), waiting for the product (every poll_until wait: OSAC reconciling a resource), test actions (the rest of the test: CLI and API calls, assertions) and teardown. A long orange segment is time spent in the product, not in the test. Population: recorded suite runs with a complete trace (a ci-observe capture whose spans are in Tempo). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent of the tests' time.

panels.title: What the tests wait for in the product
panels.description: Hours of poll_until waits by the kind of resource the test waited on, the biggest first: where OSAC's reconcile time goes, as the tests see it. Population: recorded suite runs with a complete trace (a ci-observe capture whose spans are in Tempo). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: hours.

panels.title: Tests that take the most time
panels.description: Every test by its total time across all runs. Click a test for its history and where its own time goes. Population: test results in the JUnit reports of the suite runs; a skipped test is not a run. Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above); 'vs before' compares with the $days days before. Unit: duration and percent.

panels.title: What the tests wait for, wait by wait
panels.description: Each poll_until wait, grouped by what it waits for (names and ids replaced by <id>): how often, how long, how often it timed out, and its share of all test time. Population: recorded suite runs with a complete trace (a ci-observe capture whose spans are in Tempo). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above); 'vs before' compares with the $days days before. Unit: duration, count and percent.

panels.title: Waiting by resource kind
panels.description: All the waits on one kind of resource together. Population: recorded suite runs with a complete trace (a ci-observe capture whose spans are in Tempo). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above); 'vs before' compares with the $days days before. Unit: duration, count and percent.

panels.title: Shared setup
panels.description: Session, package and module fixtures: each xdist worker sets one up once and reuses it, so its setup is charged to the first test that needs it. Population: recorded suite runs with a complete trace (a ci-observe capture whose spans are in Tempo). Time: runs created in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration and count.

panels.title: About these numbers
panels.description: What this page counts, over which window, what is missing or partial, and when each source was last written, as the API computed it. Population: the page's own population, named in the first column. Time: the window in the second column. Unit: text.
